units: B. Bath. 2ᵇ אימא מ׳ פלוגתא may I not say, m’ḥitsah (ib. I, 1) means a division of property?—Answ. רצו לחצות וכ׳ then it ought to have read, ‘they agreed to divide’.

senses.gloss: partition, wall. Ib. 3ᵃ, v. גּוּדָּא; a. e.—Esp. (in Sabbath law) a partition ten handbreadths high, to mark a space off as private ground (רשות היחיד).
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Eruvin 8:7">Erub. VIII, 7</cite> <he>אמת … אא״כ עשו לה וכ׳</he> if a canal runs through a (private) court, you must not draw water out of it on the Sabbath, unless you made at its entrance and its exit a partition &c.; <he>כותל … תדון משום מ׳</he> the wall over the channel may serve as a legal partition. Ib. 8.
Sabb. 101ᵃ, a. fr. מ׳ תלויה an overhanging m’ḥitsah (not connected with the ground).
Erub. 5ᵃ קורה משום מ׳ the beam (across an alley) serves as a legal fiction for a m. (as if its broadside were prolonged so as to form a partition), v. נְגַד; a. v. fr.

senses.gloss: divided off space, compartment; (for sacred law) camp, precinct, cmp. מַחֲנֶה.
units: <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 4">Num. R. s. 4</cite> <he>מְחִיצַת הכהנים</he> the camp of the priestly division.

<cite ref="Makkot 20a:7">Macc. 20ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>מ׳ לאכול</he> the limit (the area of Jerusalem) for consuming (the second tithes); <he>מ׳ לקלוט</he> the limit for protecting it (as having once entered the sacred precinct).
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 26:7">Lev. R. s. 26</cite> <he>עמי במְחִיצָתִי</he> ‘with me’ (<cite ref="I Samuel 28:19">I Sam. XXVIII, 19</cite>) in my division (in heaven).
<cite ref="I Samuel 28:19">Ib.</cite> <he>אין לי רשות ליכנס למְחִיצָתְךָ</he> I am not permitted to enter thy compartment.
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 20:20">Num. R. s. 20</cite> <he>מְחִיצָתָן</he> their compartment.—

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 98">Gen. R. s. 98</cite> (play on <he>חצים</he>, <cite ref="Genesis 49:23">Gen. XLIX, 23</cite>) <he>בעלי מְחִיצָתוֹ</he> his camp-fellows (brothers); a. fr.—Pl. <he>מְחִיצוֹת</he>.
<cite ref="Eruvin 89a:15">Erub. 89ᵃ</cite> <he>במ׳ הניכרות</he> when the partitions (between one house and the other) are distinguishable on the roof.
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 7">Num. R. s. 7</cite> <he>נתנו חכמים מ׳</he> the scholars fixed camps (for sacred law); <cite ref="Sifrei Bamidbar 1:4">Sifré Num. 1</cite> <he>מנו חכמים למ׳</he> (v.
Kel. I, 9); a. fr.—מְחִיצִין laws concerning partitions for Sabbath purposes, v. supra.
